# Maestro

*A free, public, homebrew class playtest for Pathfinder Second Edition. Feel free to send feedback and tell me if you enjoy it!*

*By Erik / Lucky Thirteen*

*Discord: leif13*

*Email: leaf-thirteen@hotmail.com*

*Document Version: Beta v2.1 · Playtest Version: v1.0*

You are a one-adventurer army: a brilliant tactician with a flurry of loyal soldiers at your fingertips. You wield a team of magical puppets called pawns as versatile weapons against your foes. Your creations can spread out across the battlefield at your command, allowing you to strike from anywhere at any time. With your creative mastery and tactical brilliance, you and your creations can lead the charge to victory!

## Key Attribute

**Intelligence**

At 1st level, your class gives you an attribute boost to Intelligence.

## Hit Points

**8 plus your Constitution modifier**

You increase your maximum number of HP by this number at 1st level and every level thereafter.

## Key Terms

The following key terms appear in many maestro class features and feats.

#### Pawn

A creature with this trait is a pawn: a magical servant created by a maestro. An action or ability with this trait can be used only by, or through, a Controlled pawn.

#### Controlled

A Controlled pawn is under its maestro’s influence and functions as a creature of its size.

#### Inactive

An Inactive pawn is an inanimate object: it can’t move or act.

#### Formation

An action with this trait allows multiple pawns to act at the same time. Actions that occur as part of a formation happen simultaneously unless otherwise stated, and they trigger reactions as normal. You can use only one action with the formation trait per round.

#### Range of Control

Your Range of Control is the maximum distance at which you can control your pawns. It’s a 30-foot emanation centered on your space. A Controlled pawn that leaves this emanation for any reason immediately becomes Inactive.

#### Schematic

A Schematic is a device or modification that you can apply to an existing pawn. Installing or removing a Schematic on a single pawn is a 10-minute activity that requires a suitable set of tools and a solid work surface. If a Schematic offers multiple options or modes, you choose one when you install it. Normally, a pawn can have only two Schematics installed at a time. You can remove an existing Schematic from a pawn as part of the activity to install a new one.

#### Command Spell

Certain features grant you special spells called command spells, which are a type of focus spell. It costs 1 Focus Point to cast a focus spell. Your Craft determines the tradition of your command spells. You become trained in spell attack modifier and spell DC, and your spellcasting attribute is Intelligence.

You gain a focus pool of 1 Focus Point when you gain your first command spell. You refill your focus pool during your daily preparations, and you can regain 1 Focus Point by spending 10 minutes using the Refocus activity to sharpen your mind as you concentrate on the magic that fuels your creations. Focus spells are automatically heightened to half your level rounded up. Your focus pool can hold a maximum number of Focus Points equal to the number of focus spells you have, but never more than 3.

## Roleplaying the Maestro

**During Combat Encounters…**

Your pawns let you act from a distance, filling different roles in multiple places at once. Your pawns can take on a supportive role by controlling enemy movement, providing flanking, or defending allies. Alternatively, you could focus on damaging your foes by sending your pawns to the front lines as a lethal, coordinated hit squad. Your abilities are versatile enough that the possibilities are limited only by your imagination and tactical acumen.

**During Social Encounters…**

Maestros are performers and tacticians alike. Your skill and showmanship might be apparent in the way you walk, talk, or go about everyday tasks, and they might even command a degree of respect. Depending on the nature of your Craft, you might enjoy the company of artisans, crowds, wizards, or other less-than-reputable individuals.

**While Exploring…**

Multitasking comes naturally to you. You might tinker, practice a new trick, or read your favorite book while you scout ahead or forage for food.

**In Downtime…**

You work on and practice controlling your pawns, constantly seeking to improve your capabilities with them. You might also dabble in art, performance, mechanical tinkering, or some other pursuit related to your Craft. Games of strategy are likely to be among your favorites.

**You Might…**

- Strategize with your party members both on and off the battlefield, striving to improve your coordination and effectiveness.
- Use your pawns to carry out mundane, everyday tasks like cooking or setting up camp.
- Develop an emotional or sentimental attachment to your creations.
**Others Probably…**

- Are delighted or amazed by your creations and abilities.
- Have many questions about your creations and how they work.
- Come to rely on the extra help that you and your pawns provide.

## Class Features

You gain these features as a maestro. Abilities gained at higher levels list the level at which you gain them next to the feature’s name.

#### Initial Proficiencies

At 1st level, you gain the listed proficiency ranks in the following statistics. You’re untrained in anything not listed unless you gain a better proficiency rank in some other way.

***Perception***

Expert in Perception

***Saving Throws***

Trained in Fortitude

Expert in Reflex

Expert in Will

***Skills***

Trained in Crafting

Trained in one skill determined by your Craft

Trained in a number of additional skills equal to 2 plus your Intelligence modifier

***Attacks***

Trained in simple weapons and martial weapons

Trained in unarmed attacks

***Defenses***

Trained in light armor

Trained in unarmored defense

***Class DC***

Trained in maestro class DC

#### Ancestry and Background

In addition to what you get from your class at 1st level, you have the benefits of your selected ancestry and background.

#### Attribute Boosts

In addition to what you get from your class at 1st level, you have four free boosts to different attribute modifiers.

At 5th level and every 5 levels thereafter, you get four free boosts to different attribute modifiers. If an attribute modifier is already +4 or higher, it takes two boosts to increase it; you get a partial boost, and you must boost that attribute again at a later level to increase it by 1.

#### Pawns

You have created a set of remotely controlled magical servants called pawns. Each pawn is either Controlled or Inactive. Inactive pawns are inanimate objects and can’t move or act. An Inactive pawn becomes Controlled when its maestro uses the Take Control action.

> **Take Control** ◆
>
> `MAGICAL` `MAESTRO` `MANIPULATE`
>
> **Frequency** once per round
>
> You form a magical connection with your pawns, and they become Controlled. Choose any number of Inactive pawns within 10 feet, even if they’re held in a bag or container (as long as it can be opened easily). Each pawn stands up in its space, or in an adjacent space if its own isn’t available, and assumes a battle-ready posture. This doesn’t trigger reactions based on movement. You can’t target a pawn with this ability if it has the broken condition, has 0 Hit Points, or is missing any of its original components.
>
> Controlled pawns function like creatures with the construct and mindless traits, and they can provide flanking. A pawn becomes Inactive if it’s reduced to 0 Hit Points or if its maestro falls unconscious for any reason. A maestro can release control of a pawn at any time as a free action. A Controlled pawn that leaves your Range of Control for any reason immediately becomes Inactive. When a Controlled pawn becomes Inactive, it collapses to the ground in its space.
>
> At 1st level, you can control up to two pawns at a time. This increases to three pawns at 5th level, four at 9th level, and five at 13th level. If you use Take Control while you’re already controlling your maximum number of pawns, choose enough of your Controlled pawns to become Inactive that you don’t exceed your maximum.

While Controlled, each pawn is connected to you by a plainly visible magical phenomenon, such as ethereal strings or beams of light. Normally, this phenomenon can’t be hidden or disguised by any means, and any intelligent creature can infer a relationship between you and your creations. The phenomenon is intangible, passing through or around anything that would obstruct it, and it can’t be attacked or damaged in any way.

Your pawns aren’t minions. They don’t have the minion or summoned trait, and they can act only while under your control. You and your Controlled pawns share your actions and your multiple attack penalty. Each round, you can use any of your actions (including reactions and free actions) either for yourself or for one of your pawns. Pawns can’t speak and have no senses of their own; they rely on your senses for any actions that require them (see Senses, below).

Finally, you can also Take Control as an exploration activity to have all your Controlled pawns take move actions as needed to follow you during exploration. While doing so, your pawns must remain within 10 feet of you and can’t take any actions other than actions with the move trait.

### Pawns: Additional Rules

Any pawns you create follow these rules unless stated otherwise.

**Riding Pawns**

In general, a maestro can’t ride their pawns, regardless of the pawns’ size; any attempt to do so causes the pawn to become immobilized. A pawn can carry or drag an ally as long as the pawn is one size larger than that ally, but while doing so, it can move only using its land Speed.

**Size**

By default, a pawn is a Small creature, and its body is made of 1 Bulk of the materials described in your Craft.

**Attribute Modifiers and Proficiencies**

Your pawns’ Strength, Dexterity, and Constitution modifiers are equal to half your Intelligence modifier, rounded down. Their Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma modifiers are equal to yours despite their being mindless, because they’re under your influence.

Your pawns’ level is equal to yours. They have expert proficiency in Fortitude, Reflex, and Will saves and are trained in Perception. They’re also trained in unarmed attacks and unarmored defense. They share your skill proficiencies.

Pawns gain an item bonus to AC equal to your Intelligence modifier, with a Dexterity modifier cap of +0. A pawn can use your Intelligence modifier instead of its Strength or Dexterity modifier for the attack roll of any Strike it makes.

**Hit Points and Healing**

By default, a pawn has 10 Hit Points, plus a number of Hit Points equal to 4 + its Constitution modifier for each level you have.

A pawn gains the broken condition whenever it’s reduced to 0 Hit Points. If a pawn becomes broken twice within 10 minutes, it’s destroyed. A pawn loses the broken condition after it has been successfully repaired once using the Repair activity; the DC is the standard DC for your level. With the GM’s approval, you can use a set of artisan’s tools relevant to your Craft for this activity instead of a repair kit. You can also Repair as part of the Refocus activity, performing both at the same time.

Your deep familiarity with your creations’ design lets you mend them more efficiently. When you Repair your pawns, they regain twice the listed number of Hit Points, and you can repair a number of pawns at once equal to the maximum number you can control.

Inactive pawns can still be targeted or affected by attacks and spells; they use their AC, Hit Points, and saving throws as though they were creatures rather than objects. Inactive pawns automatically fail (but don’t critically fail) all saving throws. If a pawn takes any damage while it has 0 Hit Points, it’s destroyed.

**Immunities**

As constructs, pawns are immune to bleed damage, death effects, disease, healing, nonlethal attacks, poison, vitality, void, and the doomed, drained, fatigued, paralyzed, sickened, and unconscious conditions. As mindless creatures, pawns are also immune to mental effects and mental damage.

Because pawns are neither living nor undead, effects that heal living or undead creatures can’t restore their Hit Points. Restoring a pawn’s Hit Points normally requires the Repair activity or another effect that can restore Hit Points to objects.

**Senses**

Pawns have no senses of their own. A pawn perceives whatever its maestro perceives, as though it were standing in its maestro’s space. For example, a pawn inside an obscuring cloud of smoke could Strike an opponent that its maestro sees clearly without any penalty. Conversely, if the maestro is blinded, all of their pawns act as though they were also blinded.

**Speed**

Pawns have a Speed of 25 feet.

**Magic Dispelling Effects**

Because the connection between a maestro and their pawns is magical, it can be dispelled by effects such as the *dispel magic* spell. Against such effects, a pawn’s counteract DC is equal to its maestro’s class DC, and its counteract rank is equal to half its maestro’s level, rounded down. If a pawn’s magic is dispelled, the pawn becomes Inactive and falls to the ground without taking any damage other than damage from the dispelling effect itself, if any.

**Lost and Altered Actions**

Pawns are immune to effects that would change the number of actions they receive each turn, such as slowed, stunned, or quickened, because their ability to act comes entirely from their maestro. If you receive such an effect, it also applies to the actions you share with your pawns. If you or one of your pawns becomes restricted in how you can act, that restriction isn’t automatically shared between you. For example, if your pawn became immobilized or petrified, it couldn’t move, but you could still use your actions to move. The GM resolves any unclear situations.

**Creating New Pawns**

You can create a new pawn from the equivalent Bulk of the materials specified in your Craft. Creating a single pawn takes 1 hour of work: sculpting appendages, carving runes, or performing special rites, as appropriate. You need a flat surface and an appropriate set of tools to do this. Pawns don’t benefit from any special properties of the materials they’re made from, such as duskwood or cold iron. A pawn can be used only by the maestro who created it.

**Pawns and Equipment**

Your pawns can’t wear or wield items, except for items with the pawn trait. Any item that requires investment must be invested by the pawn’s maestro instead, and it counts against the maximum number of items that maestro can invest. Your connection to your pawns lets them benefit from certain magic items you’ve invested.

- Your Controlled pawns gain item bonuses to skills from any magic items you’ve invested.
- Your Controlled pawns’ item bonus to AC increases based on the armor potency rune on your armor or on your *bands of force*. They also gain an item bonus to saves from the resilient rune on your armor or from your *bands of force*. Other permanent items that grant or increase item bonuses to AC and saves might convey a similar benefit, at the GM’s discretion.
- Your Controlled pawns’ Strikes benefit from the fundamental and property runes on your *handwraps of mighty blows*. Alternatively, you can invest a magic weapon (even though magic weapons can’t normally be invested) to share its fundamental and property runes with your pawns. You share these benefits only while you’re holding the weapon, and you can have only one weapon invested this way at a time. In either case, your pawns gain only the benefits that can apply to their attacks, with the same limitations noted in *handwraps of mighty blows*.

**Number of Inactive Pawns**

There’s no set limit to the number of Inactive pawns a maestro can have. Each Inactive pawn is its own item, with a Bulk equal to that of the materials needed to create it.

#### Formations

Formations are actions that let you have multiple pawns act at the same time. You can use only one action with the formation trait per round. You gain the Advance! action.

> **Advance!** ◆
>
> `FORMATION` `MAGICAL` `MAESTRO` `PAWN`
>
> **Targets** any number of Controlled pawns
>
> The targets Stride.

#### Maestro’s Craft

Your abilities stem from your Craft, which determines how your pawns are made, what they’re like, and the nature of your magical link to them. You choose a Craft at 1st level. The Crafts are described in Maestro’s Crafts, after the class features below.

#### Maestro Feats

At 1st level and every even-numbered level, you gain a maestro class feat.

#### Skill Feats · 2ND

At 2nd level and every 2 levels thereafter, you gain a skill feat. You must be trained or better in the corresponding skill to select a skill feat.

#### General Feats · 3RD

At 3rd level and every 4 levels thereafter, you gain a general feat.

#### Great Fortitude · 3RD

Your physique is incredibly hardy. Your proficiency rank for Fortitude saves increases to expert.

#### Skill Increases · 3RD

At 3rd level and every 2 levels thereafter, you gain a skill increase. You can use this increase either to become trained in one skill you’re untrained in or to become an expert in one skill in which you’re already trained.

At 7th level, you can use skill increases to become a master in a skill in which you’re already an expert, and at 15th level, you can use them to become legendary in a skill in which you’re already a master.

#### Ancestry Feats · 5TH

In addition to the ancestry feat you started with, you gain an ancestry feat at 5th level and every 4 levels thereafter.

#### Weapon Expertise · 5TH

Your sharp focus has pushed your martial prowess to new heights. Your proficiency ranks for simple weapons, martial weapons, and unarmed attacks increase to expert. Your pawns’ proficiency rank for unarmed attacks also increases to expert.

#### Cunning Innovation · 5TH

Just like you, your creations are constantly evolving. You make a new improvement to your pawns’ design, granting them access to a new ability described in your Craft.

#### Coordinated Strike · 7TH

You’ve honed your tactical abilities and learned to split your attention more effectively on the battlefield. You gain the Coordinated Strike action.

> **Coordinated Strike** ◆
>
> `FORMATION` `MAGICAL` `MAESTRO` `PAWN`
>
> **Targets** 2 Controlled pawns
>
> You coordinate multiple pawns to strike at the same time. Each target makes a melee or ranged Strike against a valid target, with a –2 penalty. If both Strikes hit the same creature, combine their damage for the purpose of resistances and weaknesses. Both attacks count toward your multiple attack penalty, but the penalty doesn’t increase until after you’ve made both of them.

#### Evasion · 7TH

You’ve learned to move quickly enough to avoid explosions, dragon breath, and worse. Your proficiency rank for Reflex saves increases to master. When you roll a success on a Reflex save, you get a critical success instead.

#### Tactical Opportunist · 7TH

You never let an opening go to waste. Your pawns’ Strikes have the backstabber trait.

#### Group Tactics · 9TH

Your ability to coordinate against a single foe increases significantly. If an enemy is within melee reach of at least two of your pawns, or of you and at least one of your pawns, that enemy is off-guard to you and your pawns.

#### Maestro’s Expertise · 9TH

Your foresight and sense of control over the flow of battle are unrivaled, and your techniques have become harder to evade. Your proficiency rank for your maestro class DC increases to expert. If you have command spells, your proficiency rank for spell attacks and spell DCs increases to expert.

#### Vigilant Senses · 9TH

Through your adventures, you’ve developed keen awareness and attention to detail. Your proficiency rank for Perception increases to master.

#### Light Armor Expertise · 11TH

You’ve learned how to dodge while wearing light armor or no armor. Your proficiency ranks for light armor and unarmored defense increase to expert. Your pawns’ proficiency rank for unarmored defense also increases to expert.

#### Brilliant Innovation · 11TH

You’ve learned to further exploit some of the properties unique to your pawns. Your pawns gain access to a new ability, as described in your Craft.

#### Prescient Evasion · 13TH

You’ve learned to see danger before it even arrives. Your proficiency rank for Reflex saves increases to legendary. When you roll a critical failure on a Reflex save, you get a failure instead. When you roll a failure on a Reflex save against a damaging effect, you take half damage.

#### Weapon Mastery · 13TH

Your tactical brilliance lets you get the most out of every attack. Your proficiency ranks for simple weapons, martial weapons, and unarmed attacks increase to master. Your pawns’ proficiency rank for unarmed attacks also increases to master.

#### Three Moves Ahead · 13TH

You’re always planning ahead, which makes it very difficult to catch you unprepared. You gain a +2 status bonus to initiative rolls.

#### Coordinated Assault · 15TH

You can coordinate attacks on multiple fronts with ease. When you use Coordinated Strike, you can spend 1 additional action to target a third pawn. If you do, all three pawns make a melee or ranged Strike against a valid target in range, and the penalty is –4 instead of –2. All three attacks count toward your multiple attack penalty, but the penalty doesn’t increase until after you’ve made all of them.

#### Resolve · 15TH

You’ve steeled your mind with resolve. Your proficiency rank for Will saves increases to master. When you roll a success on a Will save, you get a critical success instead.

#### Legendary Innovation · 17TH

Your creations have become the stuff of legend: worthy avatars of your superior technique. Your pawns gain access to their final ability, as described in your Craft.

#### Maestro’s Mastery · 17TH

You’re a true master of the battlefield, and your tactical brilliance is beyond reproach. Your proficiency rank for your maestro class DC increases to master. If you have command spells, your proficiency rank for spell attacks and spell DCs increases to master.

#### Light Armor Mastery · 19TH

Your skill with light armor improves, further increasing your ability to dodge blows. Your proficiency ranks for light armor and unarmored defense increase to master. Your pawns’ proficiency rank for unarmored defense also increases to master.

#### Instinctive Control · 19TH

Connecting to your pawns has become so natural that it barely requires a thought. You can use Take Control as a free action.

## Maestro’s Crafts

Your abilities stem from your Craft, which determines how your pawns are made, what they’re like, and the nature of your magical link to them. Choose one of the following Crafts at 1st level.

### Flesh Craft

Though distinct from necromancy, your Craft can look very similar to the uninitiated. Your pawns are sewn together from assorted bits of bone, muscle, and sinew to create a new, functional form. Your pawns are Flesh Pawns, with an appearance limited only by your unique imagination. You become trained in Medicine, and you can use it instead of Crafting for checks to Repair your pawns. Your pawns can be made from nearly any reasonably fresh organic material, even the flesh of animals or monsters. Harvesting 1 Bulk of such materials from a creature takes 10 minutes.

**Command Spell Tradition:** Occult

#### Stitched Together

Flesh is soft and moldable, and it stitches together easily. You gain the Battle Medicine and Stitch Flesh skill feats. You can use Battle Medicine to restore Hit Points to your pawns during battle as though they were living creatures, though this doesn’t remove the broken condition. Your pawns still can’t be healed by other effects that target living or undead creatures, including Battle Medicine used by other characters, because those healers lack your specific expertise.

#### Strikes

Your Flesh Pawns can make rancid bite unarmed attacks. These deal 1d8 poison damage, are in the brawling group, and have the deadly d8, finesse, grapple, poison, and unarmed traits. On a critical hit, the target also takes 1d4 persistent poison damage per weapon damage die.

#### Connective Tissue · 5TH

You reinforce your pawns with extra fibrous tissue. Your Flesh Pawns gain an additional 3 Hit Points per level.

#### Putrid Pins · 11TH

Your pawns are made with flesh, and bones, to spare. Your Flesh Pawns gain the Putrid Pins action.

> **Putrid Pins** ◆◆
>
> `MAGICAL` `MAESTRO` `PAWN` `POISON`
>
> **Frequency** once per 10 minutes (per pawn)
>
> **Area** 20-foot cone
>
> **Saving Throw** basic Reflex
>
> The pawn fires a spray of toxic bone shards from its body. Choose a number of the pawn’s current Hit Points no greater than half its maximum Hit Points; the pawn loses that many Hit Points. Creatures in the area take 1d4 piercing damage and 1d4 poison damage for every 20 Hit Points lost. A creature that critically fails its save also takes 1d4 persistent poison damage for every 20 Hit Points lost.

#### Blood of the Master · 17TH

Your mastery over flesh and blood lets you use your own to feed your creations. You gain the *blood of the master* command spell. Increase the number of Focus Points in your focus pool by 1.

> **Blood of the Master** ◆ · FOCUS 9
>
> `CONCENTRATE` `MAGICAL` `MAESTRO` `MANIPULATE`
>
> **Targets** any number of Flesh Pawns within your Range of Control
>
> You convert your own flesh and blood into raw magical energy and feed it to your creations. You lose any number of your current Hit Points, as long as you have at least 1 Hit Point remaining. Distribute those Hit Points among the targets however you wish, whether they’re Controlled or Inactive; each target regains the Hit Points you assign to it and loses the broken condition, if it has it. Inactive targets immediately become Controlled if eligible, following the same rules as Take Control. You can do this even if you’ve already used Take Control this round.
>
> Any pawn that regains at least 10 Hit Points from this spell gains a +4 circumstance bonus to damage on its next Strike before the end of your next turn.

### Ethereal Craft

Your Craft represents a new frontier in magical construction, one that makes other methods seem pedestrian by comparison. Your pawns are only partly made of physical materials; the rest is shaped from semisolid magical force. Your pawns are Ethereal Pawns, which have a solid physical core supporting a body of pure magical energy. You become trained in Arcana, and you can use it instead of Crafting for checks to Repair your pawns. Your pawns’ physical cores can be made from any mundane material you choose, carved with a complex array of magical symbols. When your pawns are Inactive, only this physical core is visible. When your pawns become Controlled, the ethereal part of their form manifests around it.

**Command Spell Tradition:** Arcane

#### Versatile Form

Unlike purely physical creations, your pawns can change their form with ease. Installing a Schematic on an Ethereal Pawn takes 1 minute rather than 10.

Your Ethereal Pawns have an attack form and a defense form, each of which grants them different abilities. You can switch any number of Controlled Ethereal Pawns from attack form to defense form, or vice versa, by spending a single action. Whenever one of your Inactive Ethereal Pawns becomes Controlled, you choose which form it takes.

Finally, because your pawns aren’t entirely physical, they weigh less. Each has a Bulk of 5 light Bulk instead of 1.

#### Strikes

While in attack form, your Ethereal Pawns can make force bolt ranged unarmed attacks, which have a maximum range of 40 feet. These deal 1d6 force damage, are in the sling group, and have the agile, magical, and unarmed traits. While in defense form, your Ethereal Pawns can make force bash unarmed attacks. These deal 1d6 force damage, are in the shield group, and have the finesse, forceful, parry, and unarmed traits.

#### Greater Form · 5TH

Innovative new magical arrays have enhanced your pawns’ abilities. In attack form, your Ethereal Pawns can charge their Strikes with extra power; they gain the Warp Strike action.

> **Warp Strike** ◆◆
>
> `ATTACK` `MAGICAL` `MAESTRO` `PAWN`
>
> **Frequency** once per round
>
> The pawn makes a force bolt Strike that deals one extra weapon damage die. This Strike counts as two attacks when calculating your multiple attack penalty. If the target has any circumstance bonuses to AC (such as from a shield or cover), reduce those bonuses by 2 for this attack. The Strike deals two extra dice if you’re 10th level or higher, and three extra dice if you’re 18th level or higher.

In defense form, your Ethereal Pawns stand ready to defend nearby allies. They gain the Shield Barrier action.

> **Shield Barrier** ◆
>
> `MAGICAL` `MAESTRO` `PAWN`
>
> **Requirements** The pawn is parrying.
>
> The pawn stretches its magical form wide, ready to defend both itself and your allies. As long as it continues parrying, all allies adjacent to it gain a +1 circumstance bonus to AC until the start of your next turn.

#### Resonant Form · 11TH

Unlike ordinary matter, the magical substance that makes up your pawns can flow freely across short distances, letting them enhance one another’s power. Each of your Ethereal Pawns gains a circumstance bonus to damage with its Strikes equal to the number of attack-form Ethereal Pawns adjacent to it, and a circumstance bonus to AC equal to the number of defense-form Ethereal Pawns adjacent to it.

#### Surge Form · 17TH

You’ve learned to combine your pawns to power a new form capable of gathering and releasing immense magical energy. You gain the *spatial surge* command spell. Increase the number of Focus Points in your focus pool by 1.

> **Spatial Surge** ◆◆ · FOCUS 9
>
> `CONCENTRATE` `MAGICAL` `MAESTRO` `MANIPULATE` `PAWN`
>
> **Requirements** The target is within 10 feet of at least two other Controlled Ethereal Pawns.
>
> **Area** 60-foot line
>
> **Targets** 1 Controlled Ethereal Pawn
>
> **Saving Throw** basic Reflex
>
> Your pawns channel their energy into the target, combining their magic to create a single, lethal weapon. A spatial anomaly erupts in a line originating from the target. Creatures in the area take 10d10 force damage. The anomaly is unaffected by solid objects, such as walls, and passes through them unhindered.

### Elemental Craft

Some say that art is the pursuit of nature, an idea you take more literally than most. Your pawns are made from natural materials imbued with the power of the elemental planes. Your pawns are Elemental Pawns: carved or hewn entirely from wood, stone, or solid metal. Your chosen material is intricately engraved with runes, channels, and druidic seals that imbue it with a specific kind of elemental energy. You become trained in Nature, and you can use it instead of Crafting for checks to Repair your pawns.

Whenever you create a pawn with this Craft, you must choose a physical element and a magical element. The physical element determines the pawn’s material: wood, stone, or metal. The magical element determines the type of elemental energy the pawn wields in battle: fire, cold, or electricity. Your pawns don’t need to share the same physical or magical elements.

While your pawns are Controlled, elemental energy visibly surges across their bodies. Each pawn has both of the traits that correspond to its physical and magical elements: wood for wood, earth for stone, metal for metal, fire for fire, water for cold, and air for electricity.

**Command Spell Tradition:** Primal

#### Solid Body

Your Elemental Pawns have additional properties based on their physical element.

**Wood** The pawn’s Bulk is 5 light Bulk instead of 1. All its Speeds increase by 5 feet.

**Stone** The pawn gains resistance to physical damage equal to 1 + half your level.

**Metal** The pawn’s elemental blow unarmed attack gains the parry trait, and its item bonus to AC increases by 1.

#### Strikes

Your Elemental Pawns can make elemental blow unarmed attacks. These deal 1d6 damage of the type that corresponds to the pawn’s magical element, are in the brawling group, and have the finesse, forceful, unarmed, and versatile B traits. Your Elemental Pawns can also make elemental shot ranged unarmed attacks, which have a maximum range of 20 feet. These deal 1d6 damage of the type that corresponds to the pawn’s magical element, are in the sling group, and have the unarmed trait. Both Strikes also have the trait that corresponds to the pawn’s magical element.

#### Elemental Font · 5TH

You can command the elemental energy within your pawns to spill forth. You gain the *elemental font* command spell. When you cast it, it gains the trait that corresponds to its target’s magical element in addition to its other traits. Increase the number of Focus Points in your focus pool by 1.

> **Elemental Font** ◆◆ · FOCUS 3
>
> `CONCENTRATE` `MAGICAL` `MAESTRO` `MANIPULATE` `PAWN`
>
> **Targets** 1 Controlled Elemental Pawn
>
> **Saving Throw** basic Fortitude
>
> **Duration** sustained up to 1 minute
>
> Elemental energy radiates from the target, damaging nearby foes. The target deals 2d6 damage of its magical element’s type to all adjacent creatures. It deals this damage when you cast the spell and again the first time you Sustain the spell each round.
>
> **Heightened (+2)** The damage increases by 1d6.

#### Elemental Warding · 11TH

You’ve integrated new defensive runes into your pawns’ design, allowing them to repel energy damage. Your Elemental Pawns gain resistance equal to your level to the damage type of their magical element.

Additionally, whenever you cast *elemental font*, you can designate up to five allies. They’re immune to that spell’s damage, and they gain resistance to its damage type equal to half your level as long as they remain within its area.

#### Elemental Avatar · 17TH

Your Elemental Pawns wield the full, unbridled power of the elemental planes. Their elemental blow and elemental shot Strikes deal d12s instead of d6s, and they deal 1d6 persistent damage of the same type on a hit. Furthermore, an adjacent creature that touches or hits one of your Elemental Pawns with a melee attack takes 6d6 damage of the type that corresponds to that pawn’s magical element. Your Elemental Pawns don’t take double damage from critical hits.

### Sympathetic Craft

Your Craft is born of strong spiritual or emotional ties to other people, whether positive or negative. Your pawns are Sympathetic Pawns: objects of great personal or cultural significance, often resembling humanoids or other creatures you’ve met. You become trained in your choice of Religion or Occultism, and you can use that skill instead of Crafting for checks to Repair your pawns. Your pawns can be made from any material that is significant to you, though they usually contain at least some components taken from a living being, such as hair, blood, teeth, or fingernails. Creating and maintaining your pawns often involves folk rituals, chants, rites, or other customs unique to you or your people.

**Command Spell Tradition:** Divine

#### Sealed Fate

Your pawns can latch on to another creature’s spiritual essence, intertwining their fates. Whenever one of your Sympathetic Pawns loses Hit Points, the creature linked to it by the fatebound condition (described below) takes 1d6 spirit damage with a basic Will save against your class DC. This damage increases by 1d6 at 5th, 9th, 13th, and 17th levels.

Your Sympathetic Pawns gain the Lay Bare reaction.

> **Lay Bare** ⟳
>
> `MAGICAL` `MAESTRO` `MANIPULATE` `PAWN`
>
> **Trigger** The pawn is targeted by an attack, spell, or hostile effect.
>
> You quickly command your pawn to relax its defenses and embrace harm. If the triggering effect uses an attack roll, you can choose to have the attack hit the pawn as though the attacker had rolled a success, instead of rolling. If the pawn must attempt a saving throw, you can choose to have it fail (but not critically fail) instead of rolling.

#### Strikes

Your Sympathetic Pawns can make steal essence unarmed attacks. These deal 1d8 spirit damage, are in the brawling group, and have the agile, finesse, spirit, and unarmed traits. A creature damaged by this attack becomes fatebound, linked to the pawn that damaged it.

> **Fatebound** · CONDITION
>
> Your essence is linked to a Sympathetic Pawn, and you can take damage in tandem with the pawn you’re connected to. This condition lasts until the end of your next turn. It also ends if the pawn that inflicted it becomes Inactive or if you leave its maestro’s Range of Control. Only one creature (and one pawn) can be fatebound at a time, and inflicting this condition on another creature immediately ends any other instances of it.

#### Possession · 5TH

The connection between your pawn and its victim has grown strong enough for you to influence the victim’s actions. You gain the *puppet’s curse* command spell. Increase the number of Focus Points in your focus pool by 1.

> **Puppet’s Curse** ◆◆ · FOCUS 3
>
> `CONCENTRATE` `INCAPACITATION` `MAGICAL` `MAESTRO` `MANIPULATE` `PAWN` `SPIRIT`
>
> **Targets** 1 fatebound creature
>
> **Saving Throw** Will
>
> **Duration** until the end of the target’s next turn
>
> You manipulate the connection between your pawn and its victim, compelling the target to take the actions you choose on its turn as though it were a puppet itself. The target can’t Delay or use reactions until it has obeyed your commands; afterward, it can use its remaining actions as normal. You can compel the target to take only actions you know it’s capable of, and you can’t compel it to cast a spell that isn’t on a spell list from which you can Cast a Spell. Compelling the target to harm itself disrupts your connection, immediately ending this spell and the target’s fatebound condition. The effects of this spell depend on the target’s Will save.
>
> **Success** The target is unaffected.
>
> **Failure** The target takes one action of your choice.
>
> **Critical Failure** The target takes two actions of your choice. These can be a single two-action activity.

#### Fate’s Embrace · 11TH

You can use the connection between your pawn and its victim to tug at the very edges of the victim’s existence. You gain the Fate’s Embrace reaction.

> **Fate’s Embrace** ⟳
>
> `MAGICAL` `MAESTRO` `MANIPULATE` `SPIRIT`
>
> **Trigger** A fatebound creature is targeted by an attack, spell, or harmful effect.
>
> You subtly manipulate your foe’s fate, drawing it into harm’s way. The target attempts a Will save against your class DC. Regardless of the result, the target is then temporarily immune to Fate’s Embrace until your next daily preparations.
>
> **Critical Success** The target is unaffected.
>
> **Success** The target takes a –2 status penalty to AC and saving throws against the triggering effect.
>
> **Failure** The target lets the triggering effect hit it, as though it were the target of Lay Bare.
>
> **Critical Failure** As failure, except an attack against the target’s AC is a critical hit, and the target critically fails any saving throw the triggering effect forces it to attempt.

#### Master of Souls · 17TH

The essence of life itself now responds to your manipulations. You can cast *wails of the damned* and *seize soul* as 9th-rank command spells. Increase the number of Focus Points in your focus pool by 1.

When you cast *wails of the damned*, the emanation is centered on one Sympathetic Pawn you control, and that pawn is destroyed when you finish casting the spell. When you cast *seize soul*, the spell’s item requirement is replaced by one Sympathetic Pawn of your choice. That pawn becomes the vessel that holds the target’s soul; if it’s Controlled, it becomes Inactive, and it can never become Controlled again.

## Class Feats

### 1st Level

#### Custom Armament · FEAT 1

`MAESTRO` `SCHEMATIC`

You give your pawns an additional means of attack. When you install this Schematic on a pawn, choose one of the following Strikes for it to gain, along with that Strike’s damage type:

- A melee unarmed Strike that deals 1d6 bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage. It’s in the brawling group and has the finesse and unarmed traits.
- A ranged unarmed Strike that deals 1d6 bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage and has a range increment of 20 feet. It’s in the sling group and has the unarmed trait.

#### Extra Space · FEAT 1

`MAESTRO` `SCHEMATIC`

A few changes to their design leave your pawns with some room to spare. A pawn with this Schematic installed can store up to 2 light Bulk of items in an empty compartment inside its body, though none of these items can be longer than 1 foot in any dimension.

Anyone can place an item in the compartment or retrieve one from it with a single Interact action. Opening or closing the compartment’s door is part of that Interact action.

#### Creative Discretion · FEAT 1

`MAESTRO`

A carefully planned design lets you collapse your pawns into compact, innocuous forms. While a pawn is Inactive, you can fold it into a discreet, easily carried bundle with a single Interact action. In this form, the pawn’s Bulk is reduced to half its normal value, rounded down to the nearest light Bulk (for example, 1 Bulk becomes 5 light Bulk, not negligible), and onlookers must succeed at a Perception check against your class DC to recognize it for what it is.

You can Take Control of a folded pawn without first returning it to its original form; it unfolds automatically and assumes a ready posture as normal.

#### En Passant ⟳ · FEAT 1

`MAGICAL` `MAESTRO` `PAWN`

**Trigger** A creature you can see targets one of your Controlled pawns with an attack.

You’ve learned to pull your pawns away from danger in the nick of time. The pawn gains a +2 circumstance bonus to AC against the triggering attack. If the attack misses, the pawn can Step as part of this reaction.

#### Manual Might · FEAT 1

`MAESTRO`

By manipulating the connection with your hands, you can control your pawns with greater strength and speed. While both your hands are free, your pawns’ Strength and Dexterity modifiers are equal to your full Intelligence modifier rather than half. While you benefit from this feat, whenever a Controlled pawn moves or acts, you trigger reactions in your space as though you had used an action with the manipulate trait.

#### Wires on the Wind · FEAT 1

`MAESTRO`

You’ve discovered a way to temporarily attach your magic to other objects so you can manipulate them. You can cast *telekinetic projectile* and *telekinetic hand* as command focus cantrips. Any visual elements of these spells are replaced by an effect resembling the magical phenomenon that connects you to your pawns.

### 2nd Level

#### Pyrrhic Defense ⟳ · FEAT 2

`MAGICAL` `MAESTRO` `MANIPULATE` `PAWN`

**Trigger** An enemy would damage an ally within 15 feet of one of your Controlled pawns.

**Requirements** The ally is within your Range of Control.

You understand that victory sometimes requires sacrifice. At the last moment, your pawn moves between your ally and the source of the damage and takes the damage instead. Afterward, the pawn lands in a space adjacent to that ally. If no space adjacent to your ally is available, you can’t use this reaction to protect them.

#### Advanced Advance! · FEAT 2

`MAESTRO`

You’ve improved your ability to multitask, allowing you to coordinate a wider variety of movements. When you use Advance!, each target can use any action with the move trait that it qualifies for instead of Striding, including Burrow, Climb, Fly, or Swim if it has the corresponding Speed.

In addition, when you use Advance!, you can also use a single move action available to you, using any of your Speeds.

#### Flanking Strike ◆ · FEAT 2

`FORMATION` `MAGICAL` `MAESTRO` `PAWN`

**Targets** 2 Controlled pawns

You coordinate your pawns to surround a foe, then strike. Each target moves up to its Speed using any of its available movement types. Both pawns must end their movement within reach of the same enemy. Then, one of the pawns can make a melee Strike against that enemy.

#### Canary · FEAT 2

`MAESTRO`

Your pawns are more expendable than adventurers and can serve as a first line of defense while you explore dangerous areas. While you’re using Take Control as an exploration activity, you get a check to find traps that normally require you to be Searching. You still need to meet any other requirements to find the trap. You gain a circumstance bonus to Perception checks to find traps equal to the number of pawns you’re controlling.

If you would trigger a device or set off a trap (whether because you failed to disarm it or triggered it normally), you can use your reaction to have a Controlled pawn trigger it in your place.

#### Extracurricular Crafting · FEAT 2

`MAESTRO`

Crafting is part of who you are, and you’re always looking for new ways to innovate. You become an expert in Crafting. At 7th level, you become a master in Crafting, and at 15th level, you become legendary in Crafting.

You also gain two Crafting skill feats of your choice for which you meet the prerequisites.

`MAESTRO`

You’ve learned to stretch your magical connection even further. Your Range of Control increases by 30 feet.

`MAESTRO`

This doesn’t increase the number of pawns you can control. When the duration ends, the new pawn crumbles back into a pile of inert materials.

`MAESTRO` `MANIPULATE`

**Requirements** You’re holding an appropriate set of tools, or you’re wearing them and have a free hand.

You know your creations well enough to get them back into working order on short notice. You make quick repairs to a pawn within your reach, restoring 2d6 Hit Points and removing its broken condition. The pawn is then immune to Field Repairs until you Repair it.

The number of Hit Points restored increases by 2d6 at 7th, 10th, 13th, 16th, and 19th levels.

#### Adaptive Design · FEAT 4

`MAESTRO` `SCHEMATIC`

The best tacticians know how to adapt and overcome. When you install this Schematic, the pawn gains one of the following modifications.

- **Waterproof Fins** The pawn has a swim Speed equal to its land Speed. It isn’t off-guard in water, and it doesn’t take the usual penalties for using bludgeoning or slashing melee weapons in water.
- **Climbing Rig** The pawn has a climb Speed equal to its land Speed. It isn’t off-guard while climbing, and it can Grab an Edge as a free action rather than as a reaction.
- **Subterranean Toolkit** As a single action, the pawn can shed magical bright light in a 60-foot radius (and dim light to the next 60 feet). This light lasts until it’s dismissed as a free action. In addition, you gain tremorsense as an imprecise sense within 15 feet of the pawn.
- **Additional Limbs** The pawn is unaffected by nonmagical difficult terrain and automatically succeeds at Acrobatics checks to Balance on uneven ground. It doesn’t trigger reactions when it uses an action with the manipulate trait.
- **Voice Box** The pawn can speak and use actions that require speech, such as Demoralize, as you quietly mouth or whisper the words it speaks aloud for you. Its voice sounds like yours, though you can raise or lower its pitch and volume as much as a typical person could.

### 6th Level

#### Pantomime ◆ · FEAT 6

`FLOURISH` `MAGICAL` `MAESTRO` `MANIPULATE` `PAWN`

**Targets** 1 Controlled pawn

Further study of your techniques has yielded a new way to control your pawns. You use any single action that the target can also use, and the target uses the same action.

If the action requires a target, such as a Strike, the pawn can choose any target within its range, not just yours, and it can use any of its available Strikes to match your Strike. If both Strikes hit the same creature, combine their damage for the purpose of resistances and weaknesses. Apply your multiple attack penalty normally, though you can choose which Strike happens first for the purposes of reactions and other triggers.

`FORMATION` `MAGICAL` `MAESTRO` `MANIPULATE` `PAWN`

**Targets** 2 Controlled pawns within reach of the same creature

Your pawns work in unison to impose on a single foe. Both targets attempt the same action (Trip, Grapple, or Shove) against the same creature; pawns can’t Shove a creature from opposite sides. Use the higher result to determine the outcome. If both checks are at least successes, treat the result as a critical success. Both checks count toward your multiple attack penalty, but the penalty doesn’t increase until after you’ve made both of them. If the creature becomes grabbed or restrained, it’s freed if either pawn releases its hold.

`MAESTRO`

#### Spring-Loaded Compartment · FEAT 6

`MAESTRO` `SCHEMATIC`

Adding a spring-powered launcher to your pawn’s internal compartment lets it fire the contents like projectiles. The pawn can forcefully expel one item from its compartment as a single action. If the item is an alchemical bomb or a weapon with the thrown trait, the pawn can make a ranged Strike with it using its unarmed attack modifier. Strikes made this way don’t benefit from your invested weapon or *handwraps of mighty blows*, and thrown weapons that would normally return to their owner’s hand instead fall to the ground at the pawn’s feet. Any other item can be flung to a space up to 20 feet away, where it lands unless it’s caught or otherwise stopped.

### 12th Level

#### Life Imitates Art · FEAT 12

`MAESTRO`

Your new limb grants you an unarmed attack based on your Craft.

- **Sympathetic Craft** You can make ethereal claw unarmed attacks. These deal 1d8 spirit damage, are in the brawling group, and have the finesse, spirit, and unarmed traits. This attack has the effects of a *ghost touch* property rune.

The compartment granted by Extra Space gains the properties of a *spacious pouch*, except that it can hold only up to 5 Bulk of items. Stored items have no size limits, as the magic lets your pawn stretch as needed to accommodate them before it returns to its normal proportions. If a pawn with Extra Space installed becomes overloaded or is destroyed, its internal space is ruined, and the items inside are lost forever.

#### Cornered · FEAT 14

`MAESTRO`

Your pawns are a constant hindrance to foes across the battlefield. Whenever an enemy is off-guard because of flanking by one of your pawns or because of your Group Tactics, it also takes a –2 circumstance penalty to Perception checks and saving throws.

#### Giant Maneuver · FEAT 14

`MAESTRO`

**Prerequisites** Tandem Maneuver

Through teamwork, your pawns can overcome foes of any size. When you use Tandem Maneuver, for each additional pawn adjacent to the creature (beyond the two you targeted with Tandem Maneuver), your pawns can attempt their Athletics checks against a creature one size larger than normal, and they gain a +1 circumstance bonus to those checks.

For example, if your pawns are Small and two additional pawns are adjacent to the creature (four adjacent pawns in total), the pawns you targeted with Tandem Maneuver gain a +2 circumstance bonus to their checks and can attempt them against a Huge or smaller creature.

#### Castle · FEAT 14

`MAESTRO` `SCHEMATIC`

Modified panels and a tighter body plan let your pawns shelter allies on the battlefield. A pawn with this Schematic installed provides cover to adjacent allies based on its size: a Small pawn provides lesser cover, a Medium pawn provides standard cover, and a Large or larger pawn provides greater cover. These values assume a Medium ally; the GM can adjust them as the circumstances warrant.

### 16th Level

#### Lead by Example · FEAT 16

`MAESTRO`

**Prerequisites** Air Superiority

The latest modifications to your controlling magic let you share in your pawns’ gift of flight. As long as you’re controlling at least two pawns that have a fly Speed, you have a fly Speed equal to the highest among them.

#### Beyond the Pale · FEAT 16

`MAESTRO`

You’ve stepped into a realm of artistic expression that many would consider unnatural, or even taboo. Through careful application of your Craft, you can perform a 3-hour operation that requires a stable work surface. At the end of the operation, your heart is replaced with a unique magical device. You no longer need to sleep, and falling unconscious no longer causes your pawns to become Inactive. Although you don’t need to sleep, you still need 3 hours of downtime in each 24-hour period to maintain your heart’s delicate mechanisms; skipping this maintenance has the same effects that going without sleep has for other creatures. You gain the Vital Surge reaction.

> **Vital Surge** ⟳
>
> `MAESTRO`
>
> **Trigger** You would be reduced to 0 Hit Points.
>
> **Requirements** Your prosthetic heart doesn’t have the broken condition.
>
> Your heart surges against the oncoming doom, keeping you in the fight. You remain at 1 Hit Point, and your heart gains the broken condition.

Your heart still performs its organic functions while it’s broken, but removing its broken condition is a 1-hour activity that requires your full attention.

### 18th Level

#### Dismantle ◆◆◆ · FEAT 18

`FORMATION` `MAGICAL` `MAESTRO` `PAWN`

**Targets** any number of Controlled pawns

Your pawns divide and conquer, separating their bodies into a lethal swarm of floating limbs and weaponry. Choose a burst whose origin is anywhere within your Range of Control. The burst is 10 feet if you targeted one pawn, and its size increases by 10 feet for each additional pawn targeted. The targets make one melee Strike against each enemy within the burst; enemies outside your Range of Control are unaffected. You can use any melee Strike available to the targets for these Strikes, and your multiple attack penalty doesn’t increase until you’ve made all of them. A single creature can’t be attacked more than once by this action.

After all the attacks are made, your pawns return to their original forms, reassembling in any available spaces within your Range of Control.

#### Dextrous Mind · FEAT 18

`MAESTRO`

For a brief moment, you exceed the physical limits of concentration, allowing you to precisely control all your pawns at once. You gain the *blitz* command spell. Increase the number of Focus Points in your focus pool by 1.

> **Blitz** ◆◆ · FOCUS 9
>
> `CONCENTRATE` `FORMATION` `MAGICAL` `MAESTRO` `MANIPULATE` `PAWN`
>
> **Targets** any number of Controlled pawns

> Each target uses a single action available to it. If multiple targets Strike the same creature, combine their damage for the purpose of resistances and weaknesses. Apply your multiple attack penalty normally, though you can choose which Strike happens first for the purposes of reactions and other triggers.

### 20th Level

#### Art Eternal · FEAT 20

`MAESTRO`

**Prerequisites** Beyond the Pale

You’ve taken the final steps away from your mortal shell to become the ultimate work of art. You can perform an 8-hour operation that requires a stable work surface and an appropriate set of tools. At the end of the operation, your entire mortal form is replaced with an immaculate artificial body resembling the pawns of your Craft. You no longer age, and you don’t need to eat or breathe. You’re immune to bleed damage, death effects, disease, nonlethal attacks, poison, and the drained, fatigued, paralyzed, and sickened conditions.

Your soul now resides entirely within your prosthetic heart, which controls the rest of your body like a puppet. If you would die, your artificial body falls apart instead; you don’t fall unconscious or gain the dying condition. Instead, you immediately become a Tiny creature, with your prosthetic heart as its primary component, which lands prone among the remains of your body. You keep all your abilities and statistics except your size, and you immediately regain Hit Points equal to half your maximum Hit Points. You can’t use any of the items you were carrying until you retrieve them from your remains, and any magic items you had invested immediately become uninvested. If you’re reduced to 0 Hit Points in this form, your heart and body are destroyed, and you die.

You can rebuild yourself in a new artificial body as an 8-hour activity that requires 3 Bulk of the appropriate materials.

#### Checkmate · FEAT 20

`MAESTRO`

With a well-organized attack, your pawns strike with unfathomable precision, toppling even the mightiest foes. When you use Coordinated Strike to have three pawns attack a single target and all three attacks deal damage, double the total damage (after combining it for resistances and weaknesses).
